Answers an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays, made ON THIS MAC — no network request, no upload, no API key — and kept per media in the project's cache, so a later call over a window already analysed answers at once. kind "shots" finds the hard cuts: cuts is [{frame, source}] sorted by time, frame the media's frame index and source its presentation time in the media's own SOURCE ticks (600000 per second, of the file played forwards), with count. A cut inside a gradual dissolve is not reported, and a single flash frame is not a cut; a dissolve between flat-coloured pictures (slides, title cards) can show as one cut. kind "masks" finds a person's outline in every frame (Vision's person segmentation, on the Mac) and answers its runs, never pixels: mask_size [w, h] (the masks' own size), frames (frames held in the window), subject_found (whether any frame holds a person: at least 0.5 % of the mask above half), count and runs [{from, to, subject_found, frames}] in SOURCE ticks — a run is consecutive analysed frames that agree on subject_found. Remove Background (Clip ▸ Remove Background, the Clip tab's Picture ▸ Background section, set_video cutout) draws them, and analyze_cutout makes a cut-out clip's masks and says where they stand. kind "faces" finds every face (Vision's face rectangles and landmarks, on the Mac) at 10 samples a second of source time and answers rate, count and samples [{source, frame, faces: [{box: [x, y, w, h], confidence, roll, yaw, mouth_gap, mouth_width}]}]: source the sample's instant in SOURCE ticks, frame the presentation time of the frame it read (the first at or after source, within one sample) or null; box 0…1 of the upright picture from its top-left; roll and yaw in radians; mouth_gap the inner lips' height and mouth_width the outer lips' width, each over the face box's height (gap over width is how open the mouth is). Faces are ordered left to right and carry no identity: follow one by its box from sample to sample. Values are rounded to 4 decimals; null where Vision gave none. A sample row with one face is about 176 bytes (221 with clip), so one answer holds about 296 s of samples (236 s with clip), less when more faces are in frame: read a longer media in from/to windows of at most that, e.g. 2 minutes. kind "sound_events" listens to the media's first sound track (Apple's Sound Analysis classifier, on the Mac) in windows of 900000 ticks (1.5 s) every 450000 (0.75 s) and answers window and hop (ticks), groups [{name, labels, first_class, threshold}] — laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music, speech, each the classifier labels it is the highest confidence of; none is first_class yet, so read the values as hints, never alone as a finding, and threshold is null — count and windows [{source, laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music, speech}]: source the window's start in SOURCE ticks and each group's confidence 0…1, rounded to 4 decimals, null where the classifier gave none (a window running past the sound's end). It needs a media with sound, a video or an audio file; a reversed clip is refused, since its sound plays backwards. A row is about 130 bytes, so one answer holds about an hour of windows. kind "subjects" finds people and the regions the eye is drawn to (Vision's upper-body person rectangles and attention-based saliency, on the Mac) at 10 samples a second, each sample instant also a faces sample, and answers rate, count and samples [{source, frame, people: [{box: [x, y, w, h], confidence}], salient: [{box, confidence}]}], boxes as faces' and ordered left to right, with no identity; a person box covers the head and shoulders. A row with one person and one salient box is about 177 bytes (222 with clip), so one answer holds about 294 s of samples (235 s with clip). # core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and

  bump adds its paragraph here and only the number in `format.rs`.

  `export_container.rs`

  a canvas, a duration, a rate and an override against a preset row; in an
  HLG project a video row's settings name the picture it writes as `color`,
  `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, from `dynamic_range.rs`); how an
  override is READ and REFUSED, naming the key and the value (`audio_bits`
  is 16 or 24 and only on the LPCM rows; `describe` shortens a value
  and `spelled` gives a vocabulary value's JSON spelling for any sentence
  in the crate); the sizes the sheet offers and
  `fit_within`, and `even_size` — on every row AVFoundation writes but
  `prores_4444` an odd edge resolves one pixel smaller, in the list's
  Document row (named "Document (even)") and in the resolved settings alike,
  so the size reported is the size written (G-33); and the rows themselves. In a row, `avf_preset: null` routes
  an export to the ImageIO writer (so the two LPCM rows repeat `audio_m4a`'s
  name), and `alpha` means "this ENCODING carries an alpha channel" — true for
  `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng`, false for `gif`, which has one palette index and
  no partial value — never "the canvas is translucent".
- `export_stems.rs` — an audio export's stems (spec §11 AU-107, AU-108):
  `Stem` and `Project::export_stems(StemsMode)` — heard tracks (labelled by
  `CompTrack::track`, not `silenced`) grouped per track or per trimmed name
  ignoring case, ordered, named (`Track N`, `/` and `:` as `-`, ` (Track N)`
  then ` (Track N, k)` until unique), none heard refused; read by `export.rs`.

  **Generic** — knows nothing about video; the host registers the catalog
  and a callback. Copied from Rasterize; do not add domain knowledge. Since
  road map 14 it differs from Rasterize's (a Unix socket only here; TCP with
  `admit` there), and kpgalligan/rasterize#430 offers the change. One
  listener, `start_socket` (a Unix socket at an absolute path of at most
  `MAX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES`, 103, chmod 0600, never unlinking a file already
  there), into the `serve` loop; road map 14's MC4 deleted the TCP `start`.
  **`tiny_http` 0.12's `Server` drop unlinks its path unconditionally (MC1's
  S7)**, so a socket listener records its file's
  device and inode as a `SocketClaim`: `shutdown` lets the drop run only
  while the claim `is_current`, and forgets the server otherwise; `release`

  listener — no unblock, no join — so a call in flight cannot hold a quit.

- `mcp_versions.rs` — the MCP protocol revisions (`SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`,

  codec ID → fourcc, the synthesised `vpcC`, the AAC ES_Descriptor, Opus TOC

  times by the largest reorder, audio in samples less CodecDelay,
  laced-frame times, `required_bytes`, and Vorbis's lead (the first packet's

  table, each packet's count by the overlap rule (spec §11 #228-V), with

  residues, mappings, modes); `container.rs` the first video and
  audio track and `describe`/`retime`/`sample_count`/`sample`;
  `ffi_container.rs` the six `rc_container_*` exports. The Colour
  element's MaxCLL, MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata are read too (HD-18):

  back, `mastering_from_mdcv` and `light_from_clli`, for the WebM writer) and

  `matrix` and `stream_matrix` (the first VP9 keyframe's `color_space` as a matrix code,

  is the first VP9 keyframe's header, each Opus packet's TOC and each Vorbis
  packet's first byte.
- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the twelve `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the
  eleventh `rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39: set the decoded-image cache's
  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under

  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the

  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY

  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view

  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,

each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).

  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map

  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and

  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,

  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11

  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only

- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

---
title: How tool calls behave
description: What to expect while an agent works in Frame Job. Calls run one at a time, wait for your drag, never put up a question, make one undo step each, and show in the window at once.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every tool call follows the same rules, whichever client sends it. This page says what an agent can rely on, and what you'll see if you work in the window while it does.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
  tools={['undo', 'redo', 'close_project', 'record_screen', 'get_media_analysis', 'split_at_shots', 'switch_by_speaker', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
/>

## Edits show live

An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the document as edited, and can be undone with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> like anything you did yourself. Frame Job doesn't need to be the active app for any of this.

## One call at a time

Frame Job runs one tool call at a time, across every connected client and the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/). A call that arrives while another is running waits its turn. It doesn't fail.

So a long call holds up the ones behind it. The usual long calls are `record_screen`, which runs for as long as it records, `transcribe`, and an analysis call, which can wait up to [60 seconds](#analysis-tools-wait-60-seconds-then-resume). `export` isn't one of them: it answers straight away and works in the background. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

A question the Assistant is waiting for you to answer doesn't hold up anything else. It's asked before the call joins the queue.

While a long call runs, a client's request for the tool list can't reach Frame Job either. `framejob-mcp` waits 5 seconds, then answers from its own copy of the list.

## Calls wait for your drag

A call made while you're dragging a clip, a canvas handle or an inspector slider, in any open project, waits until you let go of the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after the drag's.

There's no time limit on this wait. The call, and every call queued behind it, waits for as long as you hold the mouse button down.

## A tool call never asks

A tool call never puts up an alert or asks for a permission, so a call can't get stuck behind a question nobody can see. Where the app would stop and ask you, the call answers instead.

| In the window, Frame Job… | A tool call… |
| --- | --- |
| Offers to convert a file with ffmpeg | Treats the offer as declined |
| Prompts for a system permission | Is refused, naming the System Settings pane |
| Asks whether to save a project you're closing | Is refused unless it passes `discard: true` |
| Asks before removing a track that holds clips | Is refused, naming `with_clips: true` |
| Asks before a speed past ×12 drops the sound | Goes ahead, and the answer lists the clips under `audio_left_out` with an `audio_note` |

An edit that fails comes back as a message too. The beep or alert sheet you'd get in the window never appears. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

Anything that needs a question answered or a permission given has to be done by a person first. The rule is decided call by call: if you add a file yourself while a call runs, you still get the question.

:::note
This is the rule for clients connected over MCP. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) works under rules of its own, and asks you in its tab before it calls certain tools.
:::

### The ffmpeg offer is declined

An agent's import never shows the ffmpeg question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the file is refused with the reason. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).

### System grants are refused, never requested

`record_screen` never asks for the Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring grant, and never opens the picker or System Settings. A missing grant is refused, and the sentence names the System Settings pane. Give the grant from the recorder panel, **File ▸ New Recording…**.

A Frame Job started from a terminal runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The refusal then also names the launching process and the way out: relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or give the terminal the grant.

### Closing a project refuses rather than asks

`close_project` won't close a project with unsaved changes, and nothing is written:

> Interview has unsaved changes, so close_project left it open: save_project saves them, or close_project with discard: true closes it and loses them.

Nor will it close a window with a sheet open, even with `discard: true`:

> Interview has a sheet open on its window, so close_project left it open: finish or cancel the sheet first.

## Which project a call acts on

Every tool takes an optional `project`: the path of an open project, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out and the call goes to the frontmost open project, by window order, whether or not Frame Job is the active app.

| Situation | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| The path is an open project's | The call acts on it. `~` is expanded, and different spellings of one path match. |
| The path names no open project | "No open project is at *path*. get_project reports the open project's path; open_project opens another." |
| No project is open at all | "No project is open. Call open_project or new_project first." |

A movie opened as a project is addressed by the movie's path. A project that has never been saved and didn't come from a file has no path, so `get_project` reports `null` and only the frontmost-project rule can reach it.

The Assistant's calls are held to its own window's project. A `project` naming any other is refused.

To edit inside a nest, the tools that edit also take `scope`. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## One call, one undo step

Every tool that edits the project makes exactly one undo step, however many clips it touched. So `undo` takes back exactly one call, and the step's name in the **Edit** menu is the name the tool gives it, such as "Split at Shot Changes".

`undo` and `redo` walk the same history as <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>, so they take back the last step whoever made it. Each answers the step's name, `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the project summary, and it's an error when there's nothing to walk back. Any new edit clears the redo history.

Some tools make no step:

- **View state:** `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` and `set_scope` change what the window shows, not the project.
- **Reads:** a tool that only answers, such as `get_project` or `detect_silence`, changes nothing. So does a call that made no change, which is [safe to retry](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-no-change-answer).
- **File writes in the graphics folder:** `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic` and `import_graphic` can't be undone, and each tool says so. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).

## Analysis tools wait 60 seconds, then resume

Some tools need Frame Job to analyse a file first, on your Mac. A call waits at most 60 seconds for that, and the others wait behind it. What was analysed is kept in the project's cache, so calling again carries on from there and a part already analysed answers at once.

What happens at 60 seconds depends on the tool:

| Tool | Past 60 seconds |
| --- | --- |
| `get_media_analysis` | Refused, saying how much was covered: "The faces analysis of media 12 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." |
| `split_at_shots` | Refused: "The shots analysis of media 12 did not finish in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call split_at_shots again to continue." Nothing is split. |
| `switch_by_speaker` | The same, for the faces analysis. It only waits when one microphone is shared by several cameras. |
| `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` | Not refused. The call answers `ok: true`, an `analyzing` object and a `note`, makes no edit, and the analysis carries on without it. Call again to apply. |

`analyzing` holds `media`, the ids still being analysed, and `covered`, the share done from 0 to 1.

`analyze_cutout` works differently. It waits for as many seconds as its `wait` says, from 0 to 60, and answers the state it reached. It's never refused for time.

Keep `get_media_analysis` answers small on long media. An answer over 512 KiB is refused, naming the largest `to` that fits, so read faces and subjects in `from` and `to` windows of about 2 minutes. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Calls and Background render

An MCP call stops [Background render](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#what-stops-background-render) and restarts its wait when it edits a project or moves a playhead. A call that only reads, such as `get_project`, doesn't count.

## Related

- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)
- [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/)
- [Patches](/mcp/patches/)
- [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)

---
title: Units and ids
description: The units an agent's arguments are written in. Times in ticks, ids, track order, colours, booleans, keys that must be sent, list arguments and speed rates.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every tool shares the same units. This page is the reference for what a number, a colour or a list means in an argument, and what happens when one is out of bounds.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['get_project', 'add_track', 'move_track', 'set_canvas', 'set_transition', 'add_zoom_action', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'paste_attributes', 'copy_pieces', 'set_speed', 'add_speed_ramp']}
/>

## Times in ticks

Every time argument is in ticks, 600,000 to the second.

| Length | Ticks |
| --- | --- |
| 1 second | 600000 |
| 1 minute | 36000000 |
| 1 frame at 24 fps | 25000 |
| 1 frame at 25 fps | 24000 |
| 1 frame at 30 fps | 20000 |
| 1 frame at 60 fps | 10000 |

A time you send is rounded to the project's frame grid. Fades, and the attack and release of ducking and the compressor, are the exception: they're lengths of sound, so they stay exactly as sent.

What a time is measured from depends on the argument:

- **Most times** are timeline times, from the start of the timeline. With `scope`, they're from the start of the nest.
- **Action times** are clip time, measured from the clip's own start. That covers `add_action`'s `at`, `add_zoom_action`'s `at`, and `add_speed_ramp`'s `from` and `to`.
- **Source times** are measured in the media file, played forwards. `get_media_analysis` takes its `from` and `to` this way, not snapped to the grid, and `get_cursor_events` answers in them when you ask with `media`.

A few arguments aren't times on the timeline and take plain seconds, such as `record_screen`'s `seconds` and `analyze_cutout`'s `wait`. Each tool's table says so.

## One id space

Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space, so an id names one thing on its own. `get_project` lists them, and an edit's answer [names any it creates](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-landed-edit).

An id nothing has is answered with where to look: "No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips." A number that isn't whole isn't an id.

## Track order

`tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack and the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front.

A `track` argument is a track's id, not its place in the stack. The place is `index`, which `add_track` and `move_track` take: 0 is the back. Left out of `add_track`, the new track goes to the front.

## Colour formats

Colours are spelled differently depending on what they belong to.

| Colour | Spelling | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clips and the canvas: text, shapes, shadows, outlines, `set_canvas`'s `background` | Four numbers `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[1, 0.35, 0.21, 1]` |
| A chroma key, `video.chroma.key` | Three numbers `[r, g, b]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| A marker's `color`, a clip's `label` | A colour name: red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple | `"red"` |
| A graphic's colour props | A CSS colour string, usually hex | `"#ff5a36"` |

Three numbers where four belong, or a component out of range, is refused. Nothing is filled in or clamped. A number from 0 to 255 is the usual mistake.

A marker's colour and a clip's label are stored as written. Any name but the six draws in the neutral text colour.

A graphic's colour may also be written as `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` or a CSS colour name. Frame Job stores it as lowercase hex.

## Boolean spellings

A tool's boolean argument may be sent as `true` or `false`, or as the strings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. Anything else is refused: "discard must be true or false."

This covers a tool's own arguments. Inside a [patch](/mcp/patches/), a boolean must be a real `true` or `false`, and so must a graphic's boolean prop.

## Keys that must be sent even when null

Two arguments are required even though null is a valid value, because null means something:

| Tool | Argument | Null means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_transition` | `kind` | Remove the transition |
| `add_zoom_action` | `region` | Zoom back out to the clip's own scale and position |

Leaving either out is refused, so a forgotten value can't remove a transition or zoom back by accident.

## No empty lists

An empty list argument names nothing to act on, so it's refused by name.

| Argument | Tools | The answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | Every tool that takes one | "clips is empty — name at least one clip." |
| `ranges` | `ripple_delete_ranges`, `copy_pieces` | "ranges is empty — name at least one [from, to] pair." |
| `groups` | `paste_attributes` | "groups is empty — name at least one of…", followed by the group names. Leave `groups` out to paste the default set. |

Where a tool takes `clips`, a single id is accepted in place of a list.

A frame-rate term of 0 in `set_canvas`'s `fps` is refused too, as is a fraction: each term is a whole number from 1 to 4294967295, so 29.97 fps is `[30000, 1001]`.

Lists inside a patch are different. `filters: []` is how you clear a filter stack. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/#how-a-patch-merges).

## Speed rates are clamped

Most values out of range are refused. A speed rate is the exception: `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` bring a `rate` outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range. A rate of zero or less is refused.

On a clip with a speed ramp, `set_speed` scales every rate in the ramp, so the ramp keeps its shape, and the scale stops where any of those rates would pass the limits.

Above ×12 a clip's sound is left out of the mix. The answer says so with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Patches](/mcp/patches/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)
- [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/)
- [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)

- **Most times** are timeline times, from the start of the timeline. With `scope`, they're from the start of the nest.
- **Action times** are clip time, measured from the clip's own start. That covers `add_action`'s `at`, `add_zoom_action`'s `at`, and `add_speed_ramp`'s `from` and `to`.
- **Source times** are measured in the media file, played forwards. `get_media_analysis` takes its `from` and `to` this way, not snapped to the grid, and `get_cursor_events` answers in them when you ask with `media`.

A few arguments aren't times on the timeline and take plain seconds, such as `record_screen`'s `seconds` and `analyze_cutout`'s `wait`. Each tool's table says so.

## One id space

Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space, so an id names one thing on its own. `get_project` lists them, and an edit's answer [names any it creates](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-landed-edit).

An id nothing has is answered with where to look: "No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips." A number that isn't whole isn't an id.

## Track order

`tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack and the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front.

A `track` argument is a track's id, not its place in the stack. The place is `index`, which `add_track` and `move_track` take: 0 is the back. Left out of `add_track`, the new track goes to the front.

## Colour formats

Colours are spelled differently depending on what they belong to.

| Colour | Spelling | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clips and the canvas: text, shapes, shadows, outlines, `set_canvas`'s `background` | Four numbers `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[1, 0.35, 0.21, 1]` |
| A chroma key, `video.chroma.key` | Three numbers `[r, g, b]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| A marker's `color`, a clip's `label` | A colour name: red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple | `"red"` |
| A graphic's colour props | A CSS colour string, usually hex | `"#ff5a36"` |

Three numbers where four belong, or a component out of range, is refused. Nothing is filled in or clamped. A number from 0 to 255 is the usual mistake.

A marker's colour and a clip's label are stored as written. Any name but the six draws in the neutral text colour.

A graphic's colour may also be written as `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` or a CSS colour name. Frame Job stores it as lowercase hex.

## Boolean spellings

A tool's boolean argument may be sent as `true` or `false`, or as the strings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. Anything else is refused: "discard must be true or false."

This covers a tool's own arguments. Inside a [patch](/mcp/patches/), a boolean must be a real `true` or `false`, and so must a graphic's boolean prop.

## Keys that must be sent even when null

Two arguments are required even though null is a valid value, because null means something:

| Tool | Argument | Null means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_transition` | `kind` | Remove the transition |
| `add_zoom_action` | `region` | Zoom back out to the clip's own scale and position |

Leaving either out is refused, so a forgotten value can't remove a transition or zoom back by accident.

## No empty lists

An empty list argument names nothing to act on, so it's refused by name.

| Argument | Tools | The answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | Every tool that takes one | "clips is empty — name at least one clip." |
| `ranges` | `ripple_delete_ranges`, `copy_pieces` | "ranges is empty — name at least one [from, to] pair." |
| `groups` | `paste_attributes` | "groups is empty — name at least one of…", followed by the group names. Leave `groups` out to paste the default set. |

Where a tool takes `clips`, a single id is accepted in place of a list.

A frame-rate term of 0 in `set_canvas`'s `fps` is refused too, as is a fraction: each term is a whole number from 1 to 4294967295, so 29.97 fps is `[30000, 1001]`.

Lists inside a patch are different. `filters: []` is how you clear a filter stack. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/#how-a-patch-merges).

## Speed rates are clamped

Most values out of range are refused. A speed rate is the exception: `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` bring a `rate` outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range. A rate of zero or less is refused.

On a clip with a speed ramp, `set_speed` scales every rate in the ramp, so the ramp keeps its shape, and the scale stops where any of those rates would pass the limits.

Above ×12 a clip's sound is left out of the mix. The answer says so with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/)
- [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)

---
title: Patches
description: How an agent changes a clip's properties. What a patch merges and clears, how a bad key or value is refused, and how unknown arguments are named.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A patch is an object holding only the properties you want to change. The property tools take one and merge it into what the clip already has, so an agent never has to send a clip's whole state back.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_graphic', 'set_clip', 'set_action_end', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip']}
/>

## How a patch merges

Each property tool takes a `patch` argument. Three rules cover it:

- **Keys you leave out keep their values, at every depth.** A patch of `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance.
- **A key set to `null` clears it**, if it's a key that can be cleared. A required key refuses null.
- **A list replaces the whole list.** To change one filter, send the whole `filters` stack. Send `[]` to clear it.

```json
{
  "clips": [12, 15],
  "patch": {
    "opacity": 0.8,
    "shadow": { "blur": 20 },
    "reflection": null,
    "filters": [{ "kind": "sepia", "amount": 0.5 }]
  }
}
```

This sets the opacity of clips 12 and 15, changes only the shadow's blur, removes the reflection and replaces the filter stack with one sepia filter. It's one undo step.

Each entry in `filters` must name both `kind` and `amount`, because a list replaces whole and nothing else would fill the gap.

| Tool | What its patch changes | What null clears |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_video` | Position, scale, opacity, crop, colour and the other picture properties | `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion` |
| `set_audio` | Volume, fades, ducking, compression and the other sound properties | `duck`, `compressor` |
| `set_text` | The words and typography | `outline`, `backdrop`, and `width`, which restores auto-sizing |
| `set_shape` | Geometry and paint | `stroke`, `fill` |
| `set_graphic` | `name`, `width`, `height`, `length` and `props`, with `props` merged key by key | A prop's key, and `length`, which ends the graphic with its clip |
| `set_clip` | `name` and `label` | Either key. An empty or blank name clears it too. |
| `set_action_end` | What an action animates to: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `graphic` and `speed` | Removes the key from the end state, so that property stops animating |

`set_action_end` differs in two ways. A null there means "stop animating this", so to switch something off at the end of an action, name it in `off` instead. And its values aren't range-checked, because an animation may aim past what a stored property can hold. Its keys and their kinds are still checked. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

`set_graphic` has one exception to its null rule. If an action on the clip animates that prop, the prop is set to its default rather than removed, so the animation keeps its start.

## Patch refusals name the path

A key the property doesn't have, or a value of the wrong kind, is refused. The answer gives the dotted path, array indices included, and the value you sent. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped on the way.

| What went wrong | The answer |
| --- | --- |
| A key that doesn't exist | `unknown key "gate.knee" in an audio patch` |
| The wrong kind of value | `bad value at "shadow" in a video patch: expected an object, not 5` |
| A value outside its range | `audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21` |
| A key missing from a list entry | `missing key "filters[1].amount" in a video patch` |

A bad entry deep in a list is named by its place, such as `filters[1].kind`. In `set_action_end` the path also carries the group, as in `video.filters[1].kind`.

A refused patch changes nothing, on any of the clips it named.

## Unknown arguments are refused by name

An argument a tool doesn't take is refused before anything runs, and the answer lists what it does take:

> trim_start does not take speed. It takes clip, to, project and scope.

This holds for every tool, and for an unknown argument sent as null. So a misspelt optional argument can't be dropped in silence while the edit lands without it.

A value a tool can't read under the right name is refused by name too:

- `discard must be true or false.`
- `at must be a time in ticks (600000 per second).`
- `fit must be one of fit, fill (got "cover").`

A required argument you left out is named the same way: `Missing required argument: clip (an id)`.

## Text and shape shorthands

`add_text_clip` and `add_shape_clip` take a patch for the new clip, and each has a shorthand. A plain string stands for the one key you'd most often set.

| Tool | Shorthand | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_text_clip` | `"text": "Hello"` | `"text": {"content": "Hello"}`, the words |
| `add_shape_clip` | `"shape": "ellipse"` | `"shape": {"kind": "ellipse"}`, the kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow` |

An object works as the patch for `set_text` or `set_shape` does. Both arguments are optional. Leave `shape` out and you get a rectangle.

## Related

- [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)
- [Tools: picture and grade (set_video)](/mcp/tools-set-video/)
- [Tools: clip sound (set_audio)](/mcp/tools-set-audio/)
- [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)
